After a two-year gap, Apple is developing a new iMac equipped with the M6 chip and featuring a fresh range of colour options, according to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, with a launch expected before the end of the year.

The iMac's update cycle has never been particularly frequent — it skipped both the M2 and M5 chip generations, and a larger screen size has never materialised, as Apple has consistently steered professional users towards the Mac Studio or a Mac mini paired with a Studio Display. However, Apple is now preparing to release a new iMac powered by the M6 chip.

Gurman indicated that this update will bring "several new colours," but he did not elaborate. The 2024 M4 model only made minor adjustments to its colour palette, retaining the original seven colours with subtle tonal tweaks. The new iMac is likewise expected to go on sale before the end of the year:

This means that the upcoming autumn could be a significant season for Apple's Mac lineup. In addition to the potentially M6-powered iMac, the anticipated product line may also include: a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touch screen and tandem OLED, an all-new 14-inch MacBook Pro featuring the M6, and new Mac Studio models equipped with the M5 Max and M5 Ultra (subject to supply). New Mac mini models with the M6 and M5 Pro may also appear, though these are expected to launch slightly later.

Apple's M6 chip will be the first Mac chip manufactured using the new 2nm process, but reportedly there will be no M6 Pro, M6 Max, or M6 Ultra variants — Apple plans to accelerate the rollout of the M7 series.
